name: Hexarelin
summary: A lab-made relative of GHRP-6 that releases growth hormone through the ghrelin receptor, sold as a research chemical; human data come from a few small studies.
what_it_is: Hexarelin (examorelin) is a synthetic peptide of six amino acids, nearly identical to GHRP-6 except that one tryptophan carries an extra methyl group (2-methyl-D-tryptophan). It belongs to the growth hormone-releasing peptides, originally derived from enkephalin, and acts on the ghrelin receptor to prompt the pituitary gland to release growth hormone. It is not an approved medicine in the US.

evidence.why: Human data found here are a small study in 8 short children and a sleep study in 7 healthy men; there are no controlled trials of health outcomes.

status_us.label: Not approved; not on FDA's compounding lists
status_us.note: Hexarelin is not an approved drug and does not appear on FDA's 503A or 503B lists of nominated bulk substances, so pharmacies have no recognized basis to compound it. WADA bans it (as examorelin) in sport.

benefits.claim: Faster growth (from 5.3 to 8.3 cm a year) and higher IGF-1 in 8 short children given a nasal form for up to 8 months
Higher growth hormone through the night in a small study of 7 healthy men

risks.risk: Shorter deep (stage 4) sleep in the first half of the night, with higher prolactin, in 7 healthy men
Higher cortisol and appetite, which a review calls built into how ghrelin-type drugs work
Limited safety data, and no long-term, cancer or mortality data for growth hormone secretagogues
Black-market supply: a review reports ghrelin mimetics are sold on the black market, so identity and purity are uncertain

avoid_if: Diabetes or prediabetes (clinician first: this drug class can raise blood sugar)
Competitive athletes (prohibited by WADA at all times)

before: General health check with a clinician
labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists for hexarelin; a review of growth hormone secretagogues advises tracking IGF-1 and blood sugar for the class.

studies.title: The Safety and Efficacy of Growth Hormone Secretagogues
studies.people: Review including 8 short children and 7 healthy men given hexarelin
studies.finding: In children, hexarelin raised IGF-1 and growth velocity over up to 8 months; in men, it raised growth hormone and prolactin overnight and shortened deep sleep. The review notes safety data are limited.

studies.title: Growth Hormone Doping in Sports: A Critical Review of Use and Detection Strategies
studies.finding: Groups hexarelin with GHRP-6 and GHRP-2 as non-natural, enkephalin-derived hexapeptides with moderate effects on growth hormone and IGF-1, plus higher cortisol and appetite.

ask_your_clinician: Is there an approved option that fits my goal better?
Could it affect my sleep, blood sugar or cortisol, and how would we check?
If I compete in a tested sport, would this cause an anti-doping violation?

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence: the web-search budget ran out before hexarelin's primary studies (e.g., Ghigo 1994 on routes of activity, Laron 1995 in children, the heart studies) could be opened; findings come from the Sigalos review and Baumann 2012. The prototype's 'cardioprotection in animal models' and 'rapid desensitization' are left out because no opened source confirmed them; worth adding after checking. Seed correction: it was listed as 'investigational - in clinical trials', but no current trial could be checked (ClinicalTrials.gov pages did not load), so it is marked not approved. 'No recognized basis to compound' is an inference from its absence from FDA's lists plus the 503A rules (source 3). Structure (2-methyl-D-tryptophan in place of GHRP-6's D-tryptophan) is from source 7.
